note: Reel 27: You're the Target. Episode 5 of 'You're the test subject'. The narrator is the series voice (af_heart). The officer (o01-o09, o11) and the mother (m01, m02) are cast and placed from the cast reads (Kokoro is deterministic, so a cast read is take t1). Script 6, the back half rewritten after the user's note on cut 4. o11 is o08 again, placed from the same read. m01h and m02h are the mother's line in Hindi (text = romanised for the scorer, text_kokoro = Devanagari), only for an A/B the user may ask for. Facts and wording: docs/research.md. Read audio/vo_lab/takes/phonemes.md after every run.
ref_text: The night was cold and very quiet. Most of the street was asleep, and the lamps hummed over the empty road. Somewhere far away, a train rolled past, and then the silence came back.

lines.text: You are under digital arrest.
Do not hang up.
Would you fall for this?
Then find the three mistakes on this call.
Again. A parcel in your name.
Your pension account is frozen.
Declare your gold, madam.
Tell anyone, and they are arrested too.
That is my team.
You just looked at your door, didn't you?
Even though his badge can't spell police.
And even if it could, there's no such thing as a digital arrest.
You only know that because somebody told you.
Nobody told her.
This was never your call.
While you hunted for mistakes, your mother took off her bangles.
She corrected spelling for thirty years, and she never looked at his badge.
She was too busy proving she'd done nothing wrong.
That's not his team.
That's you, asking if she's okay.
Tell anyone, and they are arrested too.
I'm fine, beta.
You eat.
She hadn't eaten in twenty-six hours, and you went and ate.
The third mistake on this call was yours.
You'd never fall for this.
But you fell for "I'm fine."
Your real mother has a phone.
Has anybody told her?
Main theek hoon, beta.
Tu kha le.
But you fell for, I'm fine.
